note: The drawdown screen. Declared 2026-09-01, after every prediction it is scored on, so it is a backtest and is refused on the look-ahead check. Its own family of one.
The pooled fundamentals rule across all fifteen attributes. It opens the attribute-sweep family, because the per-attribute table it printed is what a sweep of that family looks like.

The same rule restricted to financials.revenue, selected after the pooled run's per-attribute table showed revenue scoring 0.1046. Same family as the sweep that produced it. Sixteen declared: one pooled variant plus the fifteen attribute-level comparisons the table amounted to. The register counts two entries in this family; the declared sixteen is larger and is the one that stands, which is the point of taking whichever is worse.

Signal: operating cash flow at or above net income for the period just filed. Event: the next reported net income at or above this one. From Sloan (1996), chosen before measurement and not from this data. Its own family of one - but it pays for sharing the SEC evidence base with four other families through the significance correction.
Signal: total assets rose over the period just filed. Event: they rise again next period. Cooper, Gulen and Schill's mechanism tested on the accounts. Own family of one.
Signal: operating income over total assets rose over the period just filed. Event: it rises again next period. Own family of one.

Signal: this filing arrived later after period end than the company's own prior median. Event: the next reported net income at or above this one. Conditions on publication timing rather than any figure. Own family of one.

Signal: a filing reporting net income at or above the previous filing's. Event: the twenty-one session return from the first close published after the filing is at or above zero. Measured 2026-09-01 on one year of prices: 22 cases, 0 scorable, because the window supplies about one filing per company. Not a null result - an untestable one.

THE SAME HYPOTHESIS, PRE-REGISTERED AGAINST DATA THAT DOES NOT EXIST YET. If the five-year price history is acquired, this is the declaration it will be scored against - written and sealed on 2026-09-02, before a single session of that history has been fetched. It is therefore the register's first genuinely Prospective entry: an event cannot have been chosen by looking at data nobody holds. It claims relatively rather than absolutely - at least a tenth of the base-rate Brier removed - because the base rate of a twenty-one session return over five years is not known today and an absolute claim would be a guess dressed as a commitment. Trial 2 in the post-filing-drift family, but on a different evidence base, so it is counted as trial 1 there: repeating a hypothesis on new data is replication, not searching.

Signal: a drawdown of at least 10 per cent from the trailing peak, split by whether the most recently filed operating income over total assets is above the cross-sectional median at that date. Event: the 21-session forward return at or above zero. The threshold and the horizon are COPIED VERBATIM from equity-price-recovery rather than chosen, so this adds one conditioning variable and no free parameters; that declaration is untouched. Trial 2 in its family, because conditioning a strategy that already failed is a second attempt at one idea, not a new idea.

Signal: most recently filed operating cash flow at or above net income. Event: the next non-overlapping 21-session return at or above zero. Sloan (1996) in its original form - the claim was about returns, and the platform's first attempt tested it against the next earnings figure instead and found -0.0074 of skill against a hindsight ceiling of 0.0002. Same signal on a different event is arguably a variant of one search, and that ambiguity is resolved against this candidate: it sits in the existing family and costs a trial.

Signal: most recently filed total assets higher than the prior filing's. Event: the next non-overlapping 21-session return at or above zero. Declared NEGATIVE because Cooper, Gulen and Schill (2008) say expansion predicts LOWER subsequent returns - the direction is fixed here, before measurement, so that reporting whichever direction happened to work is not available later. The conditional-frequency scorer is symmetric, so this direction is a stated commitment rather than a mechanical constraint, which is precisely why it must be on the record.
